Life from age 4 to 16

I like the moment somebody can take the next step without me. Helping with homework has made me curious about teaching, but I have not been responsible for a room full of pupils who all need different things at once.

  • family: Lives with his mother and stepfather; younger cousins visit frequently.
  • finances: Stable moderate income; college study would involve budgeting.
  • geography: Frisco, Texas.
  • cultureLanguages: English at home; family enjoys reading aloud and board games.
  • school: Public high school with a supervised homework club.
  • accessOpportunities: Peer-support opportunities and teacher feedback; no professional classroom role.
  • Age 4–5

    In 2014, Finley enjoyed showing cousins how to play a simple game, then became frustrated when they wanted to invent their own version. He also liked picture books about animals and building towers that rarely survived the afternoon.

  • Age 6–7

    At six, he began reading familiar instructions aloud to another child. During 2017, a teacher reminded him that explaining more loudly was not the same as explaining differently, a distinction he understood gradually rather than all at once.

  • Age 8–9

    In 2018, Finley liked both science and language lessons, especially when an example made a difficult idea suddenly understandable. He sometimes completed a friend’s task to help, only to discover that the friend remained just as confused afterward.

  • Age 10–11

    During 2020, he helped a younger cousin with schoolwork over video. He learned to ask what the cousin thought the question meant, which often revealed a different problem from the one Finley had initially prepared to explain.

  • Age 12–13

    At twelve, Finley joined a supervised homework club. In 2023, he tried two explanations for the same mathematics idea and found it more satisfying when the pupil could continue independently than when Finley simply supplied the answer.

  • Age 14–15

    Across 2024 and 2025, he continued supporting younger pupils and receiving teacher guidance. He enjoyed noticing where understanding stopped, while recognizing that a small homework group did not show him the demands of managing a full classroom.

  • Age 16

    At sixteen in 2026, Finley is exploring Texas education programs and introductory observation opportunities. He wants a steady life with time for friends rather than a very high income, and remains unsure how professional teaching would compare with the specific tutoring moments he likes.

Life now

  • enjoys: Alternative examples · Science and language · Seeing independent understanding
  • avoids: Doing a pupil’s work for them · Assuming louder means clearer
  • activities: Supervised homework club · School coursework
  • demonstratedSkills: Tries different explanations · Asks where understanding stopped
  • unfamiliarActivities: Professional teaching · Classroom management · Licensing requirements

  • struggles: Can overexplain · Limited experience with larger groups
  • supports: Mother · Stepfather · Homework-club teacher
  • practicalConstraints: Study costs · Observation scheduling · No professional experience

Still uncertain: How would whole-class demands change his enjoyment? · Which ages and subjects interest him after wider observation?
